strings.name: Navi Pillay
strings.summary: Pillay defended clients under apartheid and later served at the Rwanda tribunal, International Criminal Court and as UN human-rights chief, advancing legal responses to sexual violence, genocide and discrimination. She also chaired the inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory and Israel, whose Gaza findings Israel rejected. In 2026 she was announced as the Nobel Peace Prize laureate.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; reviewed on 15 November. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Served as an international criminal judge and UN human-rights chief, advancing anti-discrimination, judicial accountability and international human-rights protection.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Law degree, Natal (1965); Harvard LLM (1982) and doctorate in juridical science (1988).
strings.highlights.h1.title: International justice
strings.highlights.h1.text: Helped advance international tribunals’ treatment of sexual violence, crimes against humanity and genocide.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Global human rights
strings.highlights.h2.text: Served as UN human-rights chief from 2008 to 2014 and was announced as the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize laureate.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Named Nobel Peace Prize laureate
strings.timeline.t1.text: The committee announced the prize for promoting peace and international law; the December ceremony was still forthcoming.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Chaired UN inquiry
strings.timeline.t2.text: Led the inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory and Israel, until 2025.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Became ICJ ad hoc judge
strings.timeline.t3.text: Served as ad hoc judge in The Gambia v. Myanmar under the Genocide Convention.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Became UN human-rights chief
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joined International Criminal Court
strings.timeline.t5.text: Elected an ICC judge, later serving in its Appeals Chamber.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Led Rwanda tribunal
strings.timeline.t7.title: Entered international criminal judging
strings.timeline.t7.text: Appointed an acting South African High Court judge and joined the ICTR that year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed Harvard doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed her doctorate in juridical science.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Opened legal practice
strings.timeline.t9.text: Opened a Durban practice and represented anti-apartheid cases.
